key_insight: Deterministic geometric environments provide provably correct, environment-derived supervision for 3D spatial tasks, enabling models to self-evolve without the consensus-based reinforcement of their own errors. This turns procedural geometry and analytic feedback into reliable pseudo-ground-truth for continuous improvement.
problem_solved: Eliminates reliance on costly manual 3D geometric annotation and avoids the failure mode of consensus-driven pseudo-labeling that reinforces existing spatial errors in models.
method: Procedurally generate deterministic 3D geometric environments that yield analytic ground-truth signals (e.g., exact intersections, distances, occlusion labels).
Run the model inside these environments to collect deterministic feedback and apply geometric-consistency checks to validate or correct pseudo-labels.
Iteratively retrain the model in a self-evolving loop (with curriculum/domain randomization) so it improves autonomously while avoiding self-reinforced errors.
impact: Makes scalable, low-cost continuous improvement of spatial reasoning models feasible, accelerating progress for robotics, AR/VR, and 3D perception systems by replacing expensive annotation with reliable environment-derived supervision.
visual_elements: Self-evolution loop diagram: procedural environment → model action/prediction → deterministic feedback/analytic labels → model update.
Before/after overlay: ground-truth geometric primitives vs model predictions (showing correction over iterations).
Performance curve: evaluation metric across self-evolution iterations demonstrating steady improvement and stability vs consensus baselines.
Icons/mini-diagrams: 3D scene/cube, checkmark (validated labels), gear/automation to represent continuous self-training.
paper_title: SpatialEvo: Self-Evolving Spatial Intelligence via Deterministic Geometric Environments
paper_authors: Dinging Li, Yingxiu Zhao, Xinrui Cheng, Kangheng Lin, Hongbo Peng
